by: the layer and tension join, which places every principle in a cluster and resolves every tension between clusters
check.population: every architecture and lexicon record the membership map places in the cluster
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the membership map, the topology or a member record changes
check.refusal: the gate fails on a tension with no resolution, or an override that matches no live edge
check.observation: none: a cluster is a grouping of principles
check.evidence: fires-and-accepts: a suite plants a tension between two principles no layer places, and the bundled tensions resolve with no dead override
check.authority: the membership map and the topology, which a tension's resolution is derived from

records.title: Structural Core
records.intent: The architectural rules that preserve structural integrity — a single authoritative source, no shortcuts, no fallbacks, no duplication, no orphaned artifacts.
records.invariant: Structure stays sound only when every element has one authoritative home and no debt-incurring escape hatch exists.

records.title: Correctness Core
records.intent: The rules ensuring behavioral correctness and validity — no silent failures, no hidden invalidity, feedback acted on, results observed.
records.invariant: Correctness holds only when every failure is surfaced and every invalid state is unrepresentable.

records.title: Evolution Principles
records.intent: The rules governing how a system changes over time — no backward-compat cruft, no deprecation debt, no legacy retention, no 'for now'.
records.invariant: The system evolves cleanly only by deleting the superseded rather than accreting compatibility layers.

records.title: Resource Core
records.intent: The rules governing resource lifecycle and ownership — bounded lifetime, single ownership, no leaks, no implicit retention.
records.invariant: Every resource has one owner and a bounded lifetime; nothing is retained implicitly.

records.title: Execution Core
records.intent: The rules governing execution flow — a single observable path, no deferring, no dual-path branching, nothing unobserved.
records.invariant: Execution follows one observable path; nothing runs unobserved or deferred indefinitely.

records.title: Computation Core
records.intent: The rules governing computation determinism and purity — no mutable shared state, no hidden nondeterminism, reproducible results.
records.invariant: A computation is reproducible only when it has no hidden mutable or nondeterministic input.

records.title: Security Core
records.intent: The rules governing security posture — no hardcoded secrets, validated input, least privilege, no insecure fallbacks.
records.invariant: The system is secure only when every input is validated and every privilege is least and explicit.

records.title: Performance Core
records.intent: The rules governing performance discipline — measured optimization, planned capacity, no guesswork.
records.invariant: Performance is improved only by measuring first; no optimization is applied unmeasured.

records.title: Contracts Core
records.intent: The rules governing interfaces and contracts — explicit typed boundaries, versioned change, no implicit or breaking contracts.
records.invariant: A boundary is safe only when its contract is explicit, typed, and versioned.

records.title: Causality Core
records.intent: The rules governing causal ordering and time — logical ordering, retractable state, no wall-clock dependence.
records.invariant: Order is well-defined only through logical causality, never wall-clock assumptions.

records.title: Declarative Core
records.intent: The rules favoring declarative over imperative — declared configuration, separated concerns, no imperative wiring.
records.invariant: Behavior is declared as data, not encoded imperatively.

records.title: Extensibility Core
records.intent: The rules governing extension — declarative discovered wiring over hardcoded, no imperative hardcoded registration.
records.invariant: The system extends without modification only when wiring is declarative and discovered, not hardcoded.

records.title: Observability
records.intent: The rules ensuring a system is observable — emitted metrics and signals, no unobserved execution, no opaque runtime.
records.invariant: A system is operable only when its behavior is observable through emitted signals.

records.title: Enforcement Core
records.intent: The rules ensuring discipline is enforced programmatically — automated gates over convention, no discipline-only reliance.
records.invariant: A rule holds only when a gate enforces it; a rule kept by convention alone drifts.

records.title: Atomic Boundary
records.intent: The rules governing atomicity — a transactional boundary that fully commits or fully rolls back, no partial commit, no deferring within.
records.invariant: A boundary either fully commits or fully rolls back; no partial state escapes.

records.title: Human Factors
records.intent: The rules governing human ergonomics — bounded cognitive complexity, acted-on feedback, explicit approval, no unlimited options.
records.invariant: A system is usable only when its cognitive load is bounded and its decisions are approved and reversible.

records.title: Domain Modeling
records.intent: The rules governing domain boundaries — bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, no leaky context.
records.invariant: A domain model stays coherent only when its context boundaries do not leak.

records.title: Design Patterns Core
records.intent: The rules governing design-pattern use — patterns applied only to demonstrated recurrence, no speculative pattern application.
records.invariant: A pattern is warranted only by demonstrated recurrence, never speculation.

records.title: State Pattern

exemplar.before: State-dependent behavior scattered as if/else conditionals on a status flag.
exemplar.after: define state objects → delegate behavior to the current-state object → transition replaces the conditional branching

records.intent: The State design pattern — encapsulate state-dependent behavior in distinct state objects so transitions replace conditional branching.
records.invariant: State-dependent behavior is expressed by delegating to a current-state object, not by scattered conditionals.

records.title: Separation of Concerns

exemplar.before: One module mixes parsing, persistence, and rendering — a change in one ripples through all.
exemplar.after: identify concerns → separate each into one place → each concern changes independently

records.intent: The principle of separating a system into distinct concerns so each is addressed and changed independently.
records.invariant: Each concern is localized to one place and changes independently of the others.

records.title: Concurrency Correctness

exemplar.before: Concurrent access with a data race; some interleaving violates the invariant.
exemplar.after: model interleavings → prevent races → verify every interleaving preserves the invariants

records.intent: The rules ensuring correct concurrent behavior — no data races, well-defined interleavings, verified with models such as Petri nets.
records.invariant: Concurrent correctness holds only when every interleaving preserves the invariants.

records.title: Capacity Planning

exemplar.before: Capacity guessed, then saturates under production load.
exemplar.after: model load → forecast demand → provision from measured/modeled load, not a guess

records.intent: The activity of forecasting resource demand and provisioning capacity to meet it, informed by queuing theory.
records.invariant: Capacity meets demand only when provisioning is derived from measured or modeled load, not guessed.
